extracted.intended_audience: communications staff or volunteers writing press releases and public service announcements (nonprofits, organizations, churches)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for when and how to write press releases versus public service announcements (PSAs), including purpose, format/length, style, constraints, and specific checklist items for effective PSAs. Focused on producing copy appropriate for journalists/media or for public-awareness/broadcast use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release — Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to attract journalists, writers, media outlets; promotes company, product, or service; announces newsworthy events; distributed to gatekeepers (reporters, editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want media coverage or to inform reporters/editors of newsworthy company items. Emphasize news value rather than direct public-service messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits the general public; raises awareness about issues; not promoting a product/service; informs or inspires action on health, safety, community events, public welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSAs must serve the public interest first. They are intended to inform or motivate public action rather than to market an organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release — Length and Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer and more detailed (300–500 words typical); provides comprehensive information, background and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient background, quotes, and context so reporters can turn the release into a story; avoid overly short one-line notices unless appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Length and Time Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise and to the point; often limited to broadcast durations. Print PSAs 35–70 words. 15-second radio ≈ 38 words. 30-second radio ≈ 75 words. Sentences 12–15 words each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write to the time limit (15/30/60 seconds) and keep sentences short for clarity and read-aloud suitability. Edit for tight word counts to fit producers' clocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release — Writing Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use inverted pyramid structure; most important info first; 5Ws + H (who, what, when, where, why, how) in the lead; reads like a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the most newsworthy fact to appeal to reporters/editors; organize subsequent paragraphs from most to least important so copy can be trimmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Writing Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear single message; call to action focus; less storytelling, more informing; motivates public action; repeats key info (URL, phone, date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the spot on one simple idea or action. Repeat necessary contact/action details so listeners/readers retain them. Avoid complex narrative threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA Sponsorship Constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Can reference your company as sponsor/underwriter but should NEVER blatantly promote organization; if too promotional, producers/editors send to advertising; must serve public interest first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sponsorship credit only as identification/underwriting; remove promotional language, product pitches, or organizational calls-to-purchase to avoid being categorized as advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Use — Press Release (use cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases for launching a product, major company news, research findings, awards, events to be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a press release when the goal is media coverage or to notify journalists of newsworthy organizational developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Use — PSA (use cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PSAs for health awareness campaigns, safety messages, donation drives, community events, crisis information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a PSA when the primary objective is public awareness, safety, or community benefit rather than publicity for the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Public Benefit Clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Public benefit must be clear — the message should demonstrably serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before sending, confirm the core benefit to the public is explicit in the copy; ambiguous or self-serving messages are inappropriate for PSA placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Single, Simple Message
rubrics_metrics.description: PSA should communicate a single, simple message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the PSA to one action or idea to maximize retention in a short time slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Specific Call to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Call to action must be specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the audience exactly what to do (e.g., call a number, visit a URL, attend an event) and when to do it.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Repeat Contact/Action Info
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact info (URL, phone, date) should be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat essential contact or event information within the brief message so it registers with the audience and survives editing/trimming.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Time-appropriate (broadcast timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: PSA copy must be appropriate for the intended time slot (15/30/60 seconds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write and time the script precisely; use the provided word/second approximations to ensure the spot fits broadcast schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Spoken-aloud Suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: PSA must read/sound well aloud for broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for the ear: use natural cadence, short sentences, and phrasing that an announcer can deliver smoothly.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Memorable Phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use memorable phrasing to increase retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ hooks, repetition, or concise taglines that stick with the audience while avoiding sensationalism or promotional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Inclusive Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure wording is accessible and respectful of diverse audiences to maximize reach and avoid alienation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA — Audio Quality Appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio quality must be appropriate for broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting recorded spots, ensure clear recording, proper levels, and professional-sounding production suitable for station standards.
